findings.title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process check
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. SpawnProcess and multiprocessing.Process are separate subclasses of BaseProcess, so this isinstance check is false for production workers. Consequently a hung worker is never killed before its replacement starts, leaving both workers able to flush the same shards and update the same health/backpressure values if the original recovers. The same check at line 346 also prevents shutdown termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or the explicit SpawnProcess type) instead.

findings.title: Terminate remaining workers after the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the shared join deadline expires, this break skips cleanup for every remaining worker. If next_step.join consumes the timeout, no workers are handled at all; if the first worker hangs until the deadline, subsequent workers are skipped. Setting stopped only requests cooperative shutdown and cannot stop a worker blocked in Redis or future.result(). Even after correcting the process type check, these workers can remain alive after a rebalance and later resume flushing shards assigned to another consumer. Apply forced termination to all remaining live workers when the deadline is exhausted rather than breaking out of cleanup.
